utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T. The Prosector versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Before we begin, I would like to ask your leave to hand over the photocopies of the exhibits I did not have yesterday, and to ask if they be taken into evidence. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Now, while these documents are being distributed, let me tell Counsel Susak that it has been drawn to my attention that he had filed a motion on the 19th of November, '98 and there was a mishap. I don't know how it and why it -- and the way it got lost, but now I have a copy in front of me and we will take action immediately. So today or tomorrow we will grant this motion. Remember your motion of 19 November that we should ask the Ministry of Bosnia-Herzegovina to produce (redacted) (redacted). We will grant it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is there any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So they are admitted into evidence. Thank you. You are now in a position to continue. Counsel Puliselic, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I only wanted to ask the usher, we have translated the page from the booklet, the record of employment from yesterday, which Your Honour requested the complete translation. So I would like to hand it over now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Puliselic. So this will be now inserted in that booklet in the relevant document which has been completed now, admitted into evidence as a whole, including this page. Thank you. We are now in a position to move on, and I will ask Mr. Terrier to continue with this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning Your Honours, good morning witness. I would like to first of all ask the usher to show to the witness the document we were showing to him yesterday during cross-examination, before we adjourned. I believe it is document 351. Sir, yesterday we came across a problem dealing with the signatures located in this log, on one of the pages of this log. You looked at the signature and you said that perhaps it was your signature, but perhaps also it was not a forgery. In order to resolve this particular problem, I am going to produce for you the original of this document. I am going to ask the usher to show you the original after having shown it first to Your Honours and also to the members of the Defence. Witness, please hold onto this log for the time period. Have you had the opportunity to look at the section we mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the signature that is placed in reference to your own name, is it your own? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this document was established for the payment for the months served in the HVO, and in particular within military units of the HVO. Does the information in regard to your name dealing with the time in which you served as part of the HVO and within the armed services of the HVO, are those entries correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that this information was put in for everyone from the beginning of the war, regardless of when they actually were called up and joined a unit. It was put in from the beginning of the war for everyone, I think. I don't remember when I signed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember the date in which you signed this document, but do you recall the circumstances under which you signed this document and why you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think that I signed it precisely because -- well, it's possible because of the payment. I don't know. I really don't remember when I signed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you were paid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I wasn't paid because I didn't serve in the regular army, so all this -- to avoid having military service after the war, I think they put this into my regular army service record. I really don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please specify whether, when you signed this document, whether you were accompanied by your brother, Dragan, because the two entries follow one another, two are very close to one another on that page.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember when I signed this document. It must have been a long time ago, and I don't remember -- I don't remember either when I signed it or that Dragan was there. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it was a very long time ago, but it seems to me that this signature, since it concerns you, is after January, 1996, so it's not so long ago as one might think.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's possible that the signature was put there because of my military service, which I had to do, so the fact that I was mobilised in late 1993 was made use of. And I think that the date was -- for the beginning of the war was put in because it was put in for everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I am sorry, I feel I don't really understand your explanation. I am going to try to clarify, which I think is a very important point. In this log, which seems to show the time of service in the HVO, and for the purpose of remuneration, it is mentioned here that you, Goran Papic, was in the service of the HVO from the 16th of December, 1993 until the 15th of January, 1996. And in respect of this log, or this entry, you signed and you yourself have identified this signature as being your own, as being authentic. I would request that you explain very clearly for what reasons and under which circumstances you signed this log. I believe you mentioned a moment ago something about payment, which of course would be in the -- should be in accordance with this log, but afterwards I did not understand your explanation. You signed this log probably in 1996, in any case, not before January, 1996, and therefore, it seems to me, you should have some memory of the reasons for why you signed this log. Can you please repeat this explanation as clearly as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't remember exactly the occasion on which I signed this. I think that this signature was put there so that my time served in the army would be taken into account so I would not have to be a conscript again after the war. I have no idea for what other reason it could be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it stated that this was established in order to calculate remuneration for the personnel of the HVO, does that to you seem to be correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand the beginning of your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems that all of the entries were made here in this register, or in this log, in order to calculate the remuneration, the salaries of the persons within the HVO. Would this be correct or accurate?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received no remuneration from the time I was mobilised because this was counted as my military service. The people who are older than me, who had already done their obligatory military service were remunerated. Why the date put there was the 16th of March, 1993, why this date is in there, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of what you just stated, sir, would you please indicate to this Tribunal whether you know or not whether your brother, Dragan, was paid for the time period he spent in service of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether he did or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered into the service of the HVO, when you became a soldier, was there an oath you had to take of fidelity to the Croatian community?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't have to take an oath, because there was a war. There was no time for that. I was simply called up and I immediately went to the defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there no ceremony from time to time within the brigade, ceremonies during which soldiers would have to take an oath of fidelity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I took no oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let us now then go back to the first conflict, the conflict of 20 October, 19th and 20th of October, 1992. You described, during the course of your testimony, and in response to the question put to you by Mr. Puliselic, you described this conflict in very explicit terms, and I may say even official terms. You stated that the forces were trying to go to -- were trying to go to Jajce, were on the road and were stopped by Muslim forces, and that you were required to flee from your home, and that you came under fire, which came from the house of Mehmed Ahmic, and that you took refuge with your family in the woods located behind your house, the woods in which you only come out from the night before. Pardon, correction, interpreter's correction. You left only at nightfall. I would like to know now for what reasons you and your family was required to leave your household and to flee into the woods where you took refuge?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My family and I had to leave our house because, first, we were woken by intense gunfire, which confused us, and the main reason why we had to leave our house were the words we heard coming from the loud speaker on the mosque saying, "Croats, give up your weapons," and that frightened us and so we fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir, you stated that two houses and some annexes were destroyed during the course of that day. Would you please tell us where these destroyed buildings were located in the village.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those were houses which were not completely destroyed. The house of Mehmed Ahmic, Suduka, had been damaged. Drago Josipovic's barn had been damaged, Hajrudin Pjanic's house had been damaged. I think another barn or farm building was damaged. I can't remember exactly whose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that the house belonging to your neighbour, Mehmed Ahmic, was damaged, slightly damaged, not destroyed, but simply damaged. You stated that the back part of the roof, the right side of the rear roof was damaged. However, witness, it seems that after this first conflict during that day that Mr. Mehmed Ahmic and his family had to leave their house and leave Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mehmed Ahmic left his house that day and, since he was in the leadership of the SDA party, since he was an important person in that party and they immediately gave him a flat in Zenica because they were afraid something might happen to him, and that's why he didn't come back to his house, although he could have repaired the damage to his house and continued living there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct in saying that the other Muslims in Ahmici, or at least in the lower part of Ahmici, also left their house on that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they left their houses that day, but almost all of them came back the following morning from Donja Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You state they returned as early as the following morning, that is to say the 21st of October, '92?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to show to this Trial Chamber a video footage. I believe it lasts about four minutes. I would like to inform the Tribunal, as well as the members of the Defence, that this footage is an excerpt from a two-hour video which represents a broadcast from Busovaca television. The footage which I wish to show to the Trial Chamber was filmed by a television journalist from Busovaca in November 1992. The footage, first of all, shows one scene which takes place in Travnik, where one can see an HVO truck as well as various weapons, and as well as a few soldiers from the HVO, and then on that same video we can see a truck which is leaving Travnik to go to Ahmici where the truck then stops. I would wish to show this to the Tribunal and to show to this Trial Chamber what we can see as of November 1992. To my knowledge at least, this is the only illustration we have of this village before the 15th April 1992, but this is, nonetheless, the footage that we have. We will, of course, disclose this to the Defence counsel, of course, only the excerpt, and if the Trial Chamber wishes and, of course, if the Defence wishes, we can, of course, disclose the entirety of this cassette, that is to say, the entire two hours, which, in my mind, is not of interest or relevant at this stage in these proceedings. We will now submit this -- we will submit to the Trial Chamber the transcript which reflects this part of the footage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Videotape is document 352, and the transcript of the video is 352A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, of course we will see this video, but I'm curious as to why the Prosecution did not use this video when you were presenting your case and you were calling your own witnesses. How can you explain that it is only now that you are bringing out this video in response? Why are you only presenting it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I state quite honestly, Your Honour, that we were not aware of this video at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Without even being able to disclose any secrets, we wish to state that we have, about this period in respect of this same war, a large number and variety of type of information, and quite dispersed, and sometimes it is difficult and it is quite regrettable that we are not able to gather all of the information of use and of importance at the start of this trial. I think the work has been done now, but as this Trial Chamber has underscored, we could have presented this information at the beginning during our presentation of our case but I think perhaps it is better late than never, but we believe that this would be an appropriate time to do so, at the time of the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Shall we now show the film? I'm wondering whether -- registrar? Here we are. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (Voiceover) "In the direction of Vitez and Busovaca, and then we shall proceed to the locality of Ahmici, which is where partly the conflict started. We are driving past a gas station. With me in the car are Mile the driver and Vlado from the Intervention Platoon. The boys at the two four-barrel gun, Darko Predrag and Vinko Petrovic and Mladen Petrovic. This is the so-called Vitez stretch, and the area of the Croatian Defence Council or Vitez units fired from is on our right. It is the area of Rovna. Then we continue to a locality better known as Kod Picana. That is the village of Ahmici. A barricade was erected on the other side by the cemetery. We will drive past that place and film certain details. You can see Hrasno. The village of Hrasno is alive and well. The HVO units of Busovaca fired from the village of Hrasno or from Beraja, and for the many who will be watching, here are some souvenirs, scenes to be remembered, scenes which will ensure that this area becomes free. There is the mosque, partly destroyed up above, because there was a sniper there. The units neutralised it. A house. A house. Yes, gets shots of everything. And there is a tri-coloured flag flying down there. Slobodan Milosevic. Do you speak Croatian? No, Serbian. Vinko, I'm moving over to you. Ahmici, the first and the last stronghold of the Muslim armed forces, a point where they tried to stop members of the Croatian Defence Council as they were moving toward their Novi Travnik positions. After all the agreements and negotiations -- hurry up. The Muslim forces went back on all the agreements and negotiations and the response from the Croatian Defence Council is common knowledge."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the spot where the truck stopped?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where that is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the place called Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, but what exact spot in the village of Ahmici did the truck stop at?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The truck stopped at the bus-stop in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't this very close to your house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the house that we saw, the destroyed house that we saw, isn't that Mehmed Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is Mehmed Ahmic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that the roof was slightly damaged to the back and to the right-hand side, this is what you said yesterday, isn't that statement far from the reality? In other words, wasn't that statement inaccurate on your part?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, the house is slightly more destroyed than I described it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how this house, which is opposite to yours, was totally destroyed on the 20th of October, 1992? Do you know how and by whom?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know who destroyed it, but I know that it was hit by a missile fired from Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weren't there some heavy weapons positioned close to your house on that date, October 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were no heavy weapons near our house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, as have other witnesses, that the HVO forces, which were stopped on the 19th of October, 1992 at Ahmici, were going to the front to Jajce. However, you were able to hear, as we have, all of us, that the Busovaca journalists in this clip saying that the HVO forces were on the way to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time I was not able to know because I was underage and they were talking about Jajce. Whether they were really going to Novi Travnik or Jajce I really didn't know. I just know that the story was that they were on their way to Jajce, because the HVO forces usually went towards Jajce when they passed along that road. I'm not aware that they went to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, seeing this film and listening to what was said by the journalist at the end of the clip, and showing and looking at the shooting by the two black uniformed soldiers, wouldn't you think this was a rather threatening demonstration of power in relation to the Muslims of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I think yes. I think yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I should now like us to go on to another area, referring in particular to the period going from October 1992 until April 1993. You told us yesterday that your brother Dragan always maintained excellent relations with your neighbours, Muslims, but you said that those relations cooled during the last few months prior to April 1993. This Trial Chamber has heard several witnesses, Muslims I must specify, who said that your brother Dragan, in the course of that period, adopted a threatening and unfriendly attitude towards them, that he demonstrated a certain admiration in relation to Hitler, to the Ustashas, that he frequently wore a black uniform, that he was frequently armed with a sniper rifle and that he behaved in a threatening and insulting attitude toward the Muslims. How would you explain all this unfavourable testimony regarding your brother Dragan?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, he was on quite good terms at first, then they cooled with some neighbours. For example, the Causevic family and some refugees such as I mentioned Nusret Paco and many others who visited us and whom we visited until the very day of the conflict. As regards the black uniform, I told you that he received it as a present from a HOS member. It was a bit tight for him, but he would wear it only when going to Zenica. This was before the conflict. Because it was in Zenica that the HOS was founded, and all members of HOS, Muslims and Croats, wore that black uniform. As for the sniper rifle, I never saw anywhere near our house, far from our house itself, nor did he ever use any such weapon. He had an ordinary M-48 rifle that was issued to him in the forestry company that he worked for, and I have already explained why he used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to tell you also, witness, so as not to conceal anything from you, that a witness said that he saw your brother shooting at Muslims on the 20th of October 1992.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He couldn't have seen him at all because my brother was in Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the 20th of October, 1992, was your brother an HVO soldier or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you a question regarding car -- the car or cars. You told us that Dragan Papic, in April 1993, at least at the beginning of 1993, had a Zastava 101 vehicle, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What model of vehicle did your father Ivo own?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My father Ivo had a green Lada which he sold in Kruscica in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't he buy another car after 1991?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't. In 1997 he bought himself a jeep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, but doesn't a plumber have to have a vehicle in order to transport his tools and equipment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he did have a vehicle until 1991. When the fighting started he didn't want to have a car, because by 1992 and the multi-party election, and when these various armies cropped up, cars would be confiscated and stolen and he didn't want to have a car. He had just collected enough money for another car when, after having sold the other one, these armies started to be founded, and he didn't want to go through the same problems that some other people went through who had cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm not very knowledgeable about vehicles, but couldn't it be said that the Zastava resembles a Lada to a great degree, and that both these vehicles resemble an old Fiat model? Are they similar, the two of them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Lada manufactured in 1988, which my brother had until 1995, is not similar to Zastava 101. There are many differences by which you can distinguish one from the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have a photograph of that yellow Zastava by any chance?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now, Witness, going to go on to the 16th of April, 1993, referring to your testimony when you said that you were woken up in the morning of the 16th of April by gunfire, that you and your family, including Dragan Papic, left the house and fled to the wood behind your house, and that at that moment, your father, Ivo, said to Dragan that he should take his mother, his sister, and his wife, his pregnant wife, to a shelter in Rovna. And you said that as for you yourself, you, your father, and some other persons that you found in the woods, you stayed there all day, and you returned home in the evening. Could you specify the exact location of this shelter in Donja Rovna where a part of your family found refuge in the course of that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They didn't go to a shelter in Rovna. They went to Rovna because there were no Muslims there. There were only Croats there, and there were no conflicts. They stayed in an ordinary family home, and this family took them in in order to give them shelter from the things that were happening near our home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who owned this house where your mother, your sister, your sister-in-law, found shelter during that day, the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that -- I don't know his first name; the surname is Santic. I don't remember exactly. I know his brother's name is Zvonko, but I can't remember the first name of the owner of this house. I know that the surname is Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that house is? Could you point it out on a map or a photograph, on the aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The house is in Donja Rovna. I can't remember exactly. I can't point it out to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you at least specify roughly how far that house is from the Radak bridge?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The house is about -- maybe 150 to 200 metres from Radak's bridge. I don't know exactly, because I don't remember measuring anything around that house. But anyway, I think -- I know where the house of his brother Zvonko is, because I was a good friend with his sons. But I think that the brother's house was near there, and I learned subsequently that my family took shelter with Zvonko's brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in order to go to this house from your house, to Donja Rovna, you have to cross the Radak bridge? Is there no other road? Is that correct? No other way of reaching it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there's no other way, because there's the Lasva River, and the only crossing across the Lasva River is the Radak bridge, at least in that area near our house and south of the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that this house was about 150 to 200 metres from the Radak bridge. Can you tell us with greater precision what is the distance between your house, your own house, and the Radak bridge? Roughly.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe a thousand metres. I don't know exactly. I never measured it. I went there quite often, but I never measured the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you went there often, how much time did it take you? Roughly, of course. How much time did it take you to get to that house in Donja Rovna from your house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I needed about 20 minutes from my house on foot to that house, to those houses of the Santici, the Santici houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Twenty minutes to cover one kilometre? One kilometre and 200 metres?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Because you have to go roundabout. You don't have a direct route. You have to turn round the Radak bridge and then make a roundabout path. I could indicate the path from my house to Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Do that.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the path I would cover when going from my house to the Radak bridge. This is my house; this is the wood that we would go through to reach the Radak bridge. We'd go right through the centre of the wood; we'd come out here. This is the railway line that the train took. Then we would follow the route of the tracks. The line goes this way; then there's a path here that takes us to the Radak bridge. Then we cross over, and then we follow this path, and I think the houses where my family stayed are here. So you see, as the crow flies, it would be this way; but there's no bridge there, so we'd have to go this -- follow this roundabout route, and that's why it would take 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Witness, the route that you have just indicated on the map, that goes from your house to the railway line, then the bridge, and then to Donja Rovna, is the route that according to your testimony was taken by your brother Dragan, his pregnant wife, your mother, and your sister on the morning of the 16th of April; that is what you said?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now help us to resolve an enigma? We heard yesterday Mr. Ivo Vidovic, who testified just before you came. I think you know Mr. Ivo Vidovic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ivo Vidovic told the Trial Chamber that on the morning of the 16th of April, 1993, at 10 past 6.00, being in the shelter close to his house, next to Pican's cafe, that he met Nenad Santic, who asked him to take up guard duty on the Radak bridge. He arrived at the Radak bridge; he found Drago Vidovic. And ten minutes later, he sees coming from Donja Rovna your brother, Dragan Papic. And your brother, Dragan Papic, said at that moment, addressing Ivo Vidovic, that he had received instructions to guard the bridge with him. The enigma is the following: When and who gave these instructions to your brother Dragan?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know when, but I know that the instructions came from Nenad Santic telling him that he should stay at Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When could he have encountered Nenad Santic that morning?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that. I never asked him when the two of them met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the evening of the 15th or during the day of the 15th, did Nenad Santic come to visit you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No. He didn't come by. I can't remember the last time he dropped by before the conflict, and on that day, he didn't drop by at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would Nenad Santic come and visit your family, or Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they didn't visit one another. In fact, I just said that I can't remember the last time that Nenad Santic came to visit us in our house before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that throughout the day of the 16th of April, 1993, you remained in the wood behind your house, as you told us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I really did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you confirming today that you spent the whole day of the 16th of April, 1993, in the wood behind your house, the wood that you pointed out to us I think during your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I spent the whole day in the stream, actually. It is right next to the wood. There is a stream where we stayed throughout that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the translation, I see it says that you spent the entire day in the stream. What stream are you referring to? The Lasva River? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Lasva is not a stream. The stream I'm referring to is in this part of the wood. It's -- just a minute, please; let me concentrate. In fact, in this part of the wood, since we moved from this part of the wood and went down to the stream which flows this way, in this direction through the meadows, under the railway track, and toward Lasva. So we were here somewhere in this stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Would you know -- I believe you would know that another witness came before this Trial Chamber and stated that he had seen you in the end of -- or late morning of the 16th of April, 1993, accompanied by Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic, in a house, the house belonging to Jozo, which is found in the other end of Ahmici, after the cemetery. What reaction do you have to this point?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I know the witness who stated this I think did not tell the truth. Because my father would not allow my cousins and me to leave him. And I never saw Mirjan and Zoran Kupreskic. I don't remember when I saw them after the conflict; a long time passed before I saw them for the first time. I did not move in the direction of Jozo's house. We were terrified by the gunfire, and my father was terrified, and he wouldn't let us move away from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that witness stated to this Trial Chamber that they saw a heavy-calibre weapon located next to your house which was firing on Muslim houses in Ahmici? Were you personally a witness to this fact?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was no heavy weapon located near our house. This was a family house inhabited by my elderly father, my elderly mother, my pregnant sister-in-law, my sister, and I, who was going to school. These were all family houses with women and children living in them. They were not strategic positions, and there were no big or small weapons there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir, you talked with great precision, with the use of a support document, about the damages caused to your house. You said that this was caused or inflicted on the 16th of April. How can this Trial Chamber be sure that this damage was caused on the 16th of April and not another day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We really discovered this damage in the morning when we saw what had been happening; then we saw the damage to our house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am almost finished; I would like to ask you one last question, and I would now like to call upon your knowledge of the geography of Ahmici, and also your military experience, because you said you fought in the ranks of the HVO for a number of months. I would like to understand, and of course the Trial Chamber would like to understand as well: What was this guard of two or three persons on the Radak bridge? What was the military justification for this position taken by the local command of the HVO? Was the aim to repel, in your opinion, to repel an assault coming from the Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The aim of the guard at Radak's bridge was only to keep the bridge, so that there was no sabotage by the Muslims who might try to blow it up and thus cut off the Vitez/Busovaca communication. That's why people were put there, my brother among them. And there were only three of them, then a third came, and they were guarding the bridge because it was an important communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Did your brother tell you whether he had a means of communication, for example, through means of a radio?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your brother, Dragan, tell you, and do you know, whether the men who were guarding this bridge had a means of communication with their headquarters: A radio, HF radio, or any type of communication device?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They didn't have a command. It was just an ordinary man, who was the commander of the village guard, who put them there. They did not have any means of communication, any equipment for communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps isn't it, from a military standpoint, imprudent to put men at risk of being assaulted by Muslim forces equipped only with two M-48 rifles and who had no means of communication? Would it be logical to think, and should we not think, that in truth this guard was designed to prevent Muslims from fleeing through use of this bridge?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The Muslims I think -- I think there are no Muslims living in Rovna. There were no Muslims living nearby who might have fled across this bridge. As to why they didn't have any equipment for communication or a command and why they were put there without proper weapons, without equipment for communication, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure you sought to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Terrier. Mr. Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Puliselic, I would simply wish to ask if I may tender 351, 352, and 352A; I request that these be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Objection? No objection; they are admitted into evidence. Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I would first like to ask, if I may, Mr. Terrier, whether he can answer how and when the Prosecution obtained the material which was presented yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, that's a question directed to you. Are you in a position to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The explanation I may give to this Trial Chamber and to Mr. Puliselic are the following: These documents were gathered, as well as others, in Vitez at the office of the Defence in September or October, 1998, during the course of an action carried out by the Office of the Prosecutor, investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor in September, October, 1998. I can't give you the exact date, but with the leave of this Tribunal, I will try to obtain the exact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Was this a seizure that took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this was a formal seizure of these documents. Of course, I cannot go into more detail at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Puliselic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, good morning. I would like to ask the usher to show Exhibit 351. I didn't know it was already there. Thank you. Mr. Papic, the Prosecutor has shown you a list of persons signed by the head of the Defence office where, under number 4.629, is your name and your signature. You said that you didn't remember when you put your signature to this document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at this document. Can it be seen anywhere on this document when it was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't see that here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness switch on the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember to what these dates refer, the dates referring to you and listed in columns six and seven? Can you remember what these dates refer to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know what the purpose of this document is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at this second list where your signature is not there.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So take a look at both of these documents. Is it evident from these documents that they refer to some kind of service in the HVO? Do either of these documents have the name, HVO, written on them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you this now. Now, take a look at the list of persons on the document you are looking at right now. The list of persons who are members of the 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment, your name is here under a certain number. Can you look at it on page 2. It's under number 4.630, and in the previous list it was 4.629. So on this list is there at the bottom of the page a box with a commander or any kind of person in authority signing this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you whether you have any knowledge as to when the 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment was established. Do you know whether it existed in mid-1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether the 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment belonged to the regular army units or whether it was reserve unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was a reserve unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the column under number 5 it says "status" at the top of the page. So look at column 5. Have you found it, where it says "status," and most of the boxes have the letter "P" in them with a few exceptions, the whole column has the letter "P" in it. Could this letter "P" mean pricuvni, which means reserve?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think it could mean that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the list you are just looking at under number 4.643 is the name Papic Ivanka. So Papic is the surname, Ivo is the name of the father, Ivanka is the name. Is that your sister?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your sister ever a member of the HVO or of the 92nd Home Guard Vitez Regiment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, she was never a member of the HVO or of the Vitez regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now could you take a look at number 4.626, the surname is "Franjkovic." In brackets it says "Franjo" and then it says "Kata." Is that a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go on then. Number 4.627 is, "Franjic B. (Vlado)"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I haven't found this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's just under "Kata."

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I found it now, number 4.627.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Olivera," is this a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go on. Number 4.631, it says "Bosnjak, Dorde," the father's name in brackets, "Anda." Is this a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is also a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know her, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 4.632, the name is "Zeljka, Mato" is the name of the father, and "Matijanic" is the second name. Is Zeljka a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zeljka is a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then number 4.634, the surname is "Ivisic, (Marko) Mara." Is Mara a man's name or a woman's name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mara is a woman's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 4.635, the surname is "Safradin," in brackets the father's name is "Marko," and then the name is "Marinka." Is Marinka a man or a woman? What kind of name is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's a woman's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said that your sister, Ivanka, was never a member of the HVO, nor of the 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, she was never a member of the HVO or of the Vitez regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now take a look at column number 4. Look at this column. In only three places has it been filled in and the heading is a number of military identity card or military booklet. What can you conclude from this entire column, because the number of military booklet is not entered anywhere?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can conclude that only three of these people have a military booklet out of this whole list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next the name of your brother, Papic, Ivo Dragan. Is there a registry number of the military book?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If your brother, Dragan, was employed in the forestry until the beginning of the war, could he have at the same time belonged to a regular military unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he couldn't have belonged to a military unit because he had a regular job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether all those who were employed and who were of military age, whether they were listed as reserve soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were all reserve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about shares being distributed in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about the shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what people did or what was done to get as many shares as possible? Was precedence in distributing these shares after their privatization given to those who, for example, had worked for a longer time or who had done more service in a military unit? Those who had served in the army longer, was this an advantage?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was an advantage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was an advantage for getting shares?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, those who had done more military service were given more shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it sometimes happen, because of this, that people somehow tried to represent that they had been members of military units for a longer time than they had actually been?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think that those who were able to do that did it, but I don't have any exact information about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this, perhaps, the reason why there are so many people on these lists, over four and a half thousand people in the Vitez municipality, with even women on the lists? Could that be the reason for these lists? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of this, but it's possible. However, I have no detailed or precise information about this, and I can't explain it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall now go on to the date, 20th of October, 1992. Do you have any knowledge that shots were fired on that morning from some kind of weapon at Pero Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, an infantry weapon was used to shoot at his house. There was probably some damage to his house, yes, there was damage on the outside of the house and in the rooms as well, and the windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier asked you when, after this conflict on the 20th of October, 1992, the Muslims returned to Ahmici. You said then that the Muslims from lower Ahmici had returned the next morning?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am now asking you, the rest of the Muslims from Ahmici who had fled, whether they also returned the next day or whether they returned over the next few days?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Perhaps. I don't know. I can't answer that question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know only about the Muslims from lower Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, about the ones from lower Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would now like to ask that the video, Prosecution Exhibit 352, be shown again. I would like to stop at Mehmed Ahmic's house. Perhaps we could do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Let's take a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Before we see the video clip presented by the Prosecution, Exhibit 352, I should like to ask Mr. Terrier whether he could say how we can tell that the video was taken on the 20th of October, 1992. Is there any evidence to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes. At the very beginning of the tape, according to the translation of the words spoken by the reporter, it was taken on the 7th of November, 1992, and to prove this I will communicate and disclose to the Defence the whole tape. It is quite evident that it is after the 20th of October and before the 16th of April, because we see the minaret which is still standing in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could we now play the tape again, and could we stop when we reach Mehmed Ahmic's house, please? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Stop, please. Just wind it back a little, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, is this Mehmed Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can't see the shot. I should now like to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit 61. Usher, please. Mr. Papic, is there any difference between these two photographs? Which photograph shows the greater damage, the shot from the videotape and this photograph on -- that is, the Prosecutor's exhibit is more lacking on the house than on the house shown on the videotape?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So here the house damaged more?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please show us the shot from the tape, please, on the screen? Can the damage be seen from a heavy weapon such as an anti-aircraft machine gun or a gun? Do you know the kind of damage provoked by a heavy weapon when it hits a house? Does it leave holes or does it destroy walls?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It leaves holes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on this picture any holes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Are you referring to this still from the videotape?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one on the screen. Will you look at the front of this building, the windows and the doors? Can you see anywhere holes such as those that would be provoked by an anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know the kind of damage provoked by such a heavy weapon as an anti-aircraft gun? It makes big penetrating holes through the walls?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I should now like to go on to another question. When your -- when one wants to go to Jajce, do you pass by Travnik?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. When you're going to Jajce -- from Jajce you pass through Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question by Mr. Terrier, you said that on the 16th of April, when he asked you where you were hiding on that day, you said that you were hiding in the wood in the immediate neighbourhood of your house and that you went to some kind of a stream. That's what you said, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you imply when you use the word "stream?" Is it a kind of hollow or is it a hollow with water flowing through it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is a hollow with water flowing through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I know that I should not have any questions for the witness, but I just wish to ask the Prosecutor two questions before we proceed with the next witness. From the documents he gave us today consisting of these lists of military conscripts, it is evident that there are a large number of names, 4.656, in fact, but it seems to me that we were not given the whole document but only a part of it. I didn't wish to object when this was admitted into evidence, but in any event, unless the Prosecutor gives us the whole document I would object as to its authenticity. That is why I think that they should supply us with the whole document, because, among other things, I believe that the document will come up again during the examination of other witnesses, so as not to find ourselves in the position that my colleague, Defence counsel for Mr. Papic, found himself in today. And as the Prosecutor has the complete document, we would like to ask that it be disclosed to us. The same applies to the videotape. Only the part was shown which the Prosecutor considers suits his case, but we would like to see the whole recording, because there may be certain details that could be of assistance to the Defence. So could the Trial Chamber ask the Prosecution to provide us with the complete document and the complete videotape?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, regarding the tape, I said and I confirm that we will communicate to the Trial Chamber and the Defence the whole tape lasting two and a half hours and originating from Busovaca television. As for the ledger that we reviewed yesterday and today, Mr. Radovic seems to be convinced that it will come up again in another stage of this trial. All I can say is that in accordance with the instructions of this Trial Chamber, before the cross-examination and before the appearance of a particular witness, if we intend to use this ledger we will provide a copy, the whole copy, to the Defence. That is, all the pages of this ledger. But today, regardless of what the opinion of Mr. Radovic may be, I cannot say that we will use it. I also cannot say that we won't use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I apologise. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, you intended to say a few things?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for trying to interrupt you. I just wanted to say that in this way we are prolonging the presentation of evidence. The Prosecution presented its evidence in the first stage. If necessary, we will have to consider whether we need to call another witness in connection with this document, and this can go on indefinitely. In order to know what kind of document it is, we need the whole document. Furthermore, yesterday you noted that as a -- a document that is tendered into evidence has to be complete and fully translated. That is why the occupational booklet was not admitted into evidence. So that is the other reason why we feel that the Prosecutor is duty-bound to provide us with the complete document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Our ruling is that the Prosecution should disclose the whole document today or tomorrow. I mean, as soon as it is available. The whole document. We can't allow only one part of the document to be disclosed to the Defence. So -- translated, yes. The relevant parts will be translated into English and the whole document shall be disclosed to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the translation has already been made. We communicated that together with the original. The translation of the first page, the heading of each column, the cover page, so that we know what it is about, as well as the page that we wanted to use in the course of this cross-examination. So the point is to make it clear what it is about for Mr. Puliselic to be able to continue with his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But we wish to have the whole document, and if there are parts that need to be translated it needs to be done. Otherwise, you can just provide a photocopy of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is rather a thick document. I would like to ask to be given a little more time, at least until next week to produce it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So decided, and we can move on. We have no questions for Mr. Papic. Mr. Papic -- Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to finish with this document, we will be satisfied if the Prosecutor gives us the document before we resume hearings next time. So it need not be tomorrow. I hope that is more convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume our hearings, I think on Wednesday. So, say, by Tuesday. If you can disclose this document to the Defence by Tuesday -- or next week. All right. Mr. Papic, thank you for giving evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We shall move on to our next witness. I understand no protective measures have been requested for Mr. Santic, so we will now call Mr. Santic. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Solemn declaration: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic? Examined by Mr. Puliselic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please introduce yourself to the Court, your name -- you may be seated -- where you were born and where you're living.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: My name is Zvonimir Santic, born on the 4th of September, 1939 in Donja Rovna, Busovaca municipality, and that is where I'm living today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, to your right-hand side is a small picture, a small easel. Could you indicate Donja Rovna on that aerial photograph for us, please? Take the pointer with you. Would you please turn around for Their Honours to be able to see?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Roughly here. This area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may go back to your seat. Mr. Santic, which municipality does Donja Rovna belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Donja Rovna belongs to Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Muslims living in Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far Ahmici is from Donja Rovna, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: About 700 to 800 metres. Up to 1.000 on the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What side of the Lasva River is Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which are the closest Muslim villages to yours in Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: The closest Muslim villages are Kovacevac, Pezici, and Gornja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please point on the larger picture those places with the pointer, please, if they are indicated; if not, just roughly where they are. Find Donja Rovna first, and then point to Gornja Rovna, or Upper Rovna --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I apologise; I need my spectacles. Gornja Rovna, or Upper Rovna, is roughly here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it indicated on the map? Can you see the words there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, no, there is no inscription. Only for Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the other Muslim villages, please.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: This is Donja Rovna, Gornja Rovna, Pezici, and Kovacevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Where were you employed in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: In the Mediapan factory in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "Mediapan factory"; what does that factory manufacture?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: The factory used to produce Mediapan wooden boards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they used for?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: For furniture and for various other purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you were a member of the village guards, and if you were, from when?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I was, around April 1992/93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the purpose of those guards was?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: It was mostly to protect the villages from the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was at the beginning, in 1992, when those guards were first formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you all, or some of you, have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There were very few uniforms. I don't remember, really. Maybe one or two persons had camouflage jackets, but no one had real uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There was a hunting rifle and one M-48 rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the first conflict between the Croats and Muslims, the conflict that occurred on the 20th of October, 1992? Was there an exchange of fire, where were you, and so on.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: In the morning, at 5.20, which is the normal time I leave for work, I reached the Radak bridge, I crossed the Lasva River, and then I suddenly heard very strong gunfire in the direction of Ahmici. I didn't know anything at the time; I had no idea what was happening. I thought to myself, should I go to work or not? And then I went back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you go to work, you go on foot?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I go on foot to -- up to the area of Santici, where there are some Muslims as well, and there was a bus stop there where we caught the bus to go to work, and that is where we came back from work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it when you heard the gunfire?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: It could have been about 5.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that day you didn't go to work?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, did you find out what happened and where the shooting had come from and what the cause of the conflict was? Did you learn about that later?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I didn't see -- I cannot tell the whole truth, but I heard from others that the Muslims somewhere near the Catholic cemetery had built some roadblocks, they had dug trenches; that is what I heard that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that barricade provoke? How did the conflict occur?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: As far as I was informed about it, the HVO had left from Busovaca and Kiseljak to go to Jajce to defend the lines from the JNA and the Serb people in Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To reach Jajce, do you know that you have to pass through Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you had to pass through Stari Travnik, or Old Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that any one of the Croats living in Ahmici, the Croat inhabitants of Ahmici, did you hear of any one of them participating in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that. Nobody told me about that, nor did I hear about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see him here in the courtroom, over there, near the wall?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I saw him as I was going towards my house that morning. It was about 8.00. Dragan was wearing an M-60 mortar and a bag. So I -- we said hello, and I asked him, "What's happening, Dragan? And he said "I don't know, but there appears to be a conflict between the Croats and the Muslims." Then I asked him, "But how is that? Where are you going?" And then he said "Nenad Santic had given me orders to go to Njive."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he had learned to use such a small mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: In fact, I asked him, and he told me that he had been trained to use it in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he told you that Nenad Santic had sent him to go to Njive? On the smaller photograph, can you point to Njive for us, please? First find Radak's bridge, and then Donja Rovna, your house.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Njive are in this area here. My house is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is your house. So Njive -- how far away from your house?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: About 100 to 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You can sit down. What did Dragan Papic say to you? What was he going to do in Njive?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: He said that if there was an attack from the southern side, the three Muslim villages, to prevent them from entering Donja Rovna, he was to offer some kind of resistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you hear that Dragan Papic used the mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he had used it, would you have heard it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Of course I would have heard it. I went to Njive two or three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of Donja Rovna, was there any gunfire?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There was no gunfire from any kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when was Dragan Papic in Njive on that day, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Approximately about 4 p.m., approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you meet him again?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he came to my house on his way back from Njive, and he told me that Nenad Santic had told him that the mortar and the bag he was carrying should stay in my house, and that Nenad would send someone to pick up the mortar and the bag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did someone come to pick up these things?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not immediately. Two or three days later someone came. I don't know who; I was at work. But my wife told me that the mortar had been taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how Dragan Papic was dressed on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: On that day, as far as I can remember, Dragan Papic may have been wearing a camouflage uniform, and I don't know what kind of trousers he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any insignia on the jacket?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No. Not that I remember. I don't believe there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in January 1993, that is in early 1993, there was an armed conflict between the army of B and H and the HVO in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I heard that. I wasn't there, but I heard that that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, were you perhaps involved in the village guards more intensely?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, we stepped up the guards, and we patrolled at night and by day, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your role in these guards?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of a squad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A squad of the village guards?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened on the 15th of April, 1993, the day before the armed conflict? Did anything special happen? Was there any suggestion that such a major conflict might break out the following day?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Personally, I had no idea. I knew nothing, nor did I hear from anyone that something like that might happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when the gunfire started on the 16th of April, 1993, at what time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Around 6 a.m. That's when the gunfire started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you see Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Dragan Papic on that day. I was at Radak's bridge then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he alone, or with someone?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Dragan went with his wife, his mother, and his sister. And he was carrying a bag, some things; I have no idea what they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice or know that Dragan's wife was pregnant?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I didn't know, but I could see that she was pregnant and that she was in an advanced state of pregnancy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from this family, did you see any other families arriving to Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Two, three families had already come. Many people came to Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember, or do you know, where Dragan Papic took his family for shelter?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: He asked if he could put them in my house, but I said I already had two families staying with me, so we put them in my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your brother's name?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: My brother's name is Anto Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you see Dragan Papic again?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, after about ten minutes, he came back to the bridge and crossed over to the left bank, and Ivo Vidovic and Dragan Vidovic were already there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: They were keeping guard to prevent a sabotage unit coming to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were on the right side?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was on the right side of the bridge with three other men who were there with me guarding the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Dragan Papic there on the following days, guarding the bridge on the other side?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Dragan was there seven, eight, ten days; I don't know exactly. But I'm sure he was there at least seven or eight days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he or anybody else left the guard especially in those first few days? Could they leave that spot?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No one could leave that spot because there was gunfire, you couldn't go anywhere. Those who were in the trenches were there, and those who were not in the trenches were in shelters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have a shelter?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: They had a shelter in the house of the late Pero Ljubas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to come.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D23/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, on this map you can see an aerial photograph of the broader region of Ahmici. This is the same photograph on the panel, only smaller.
