You have a red felt tipped pen here somewhere. Please take it. Could you find your house in Donja Rovna and put a circle around it. Could you mark it "1." Then mark the fields, put number "2" there, or Njive, sorry, not the fields, Njive. Then circle Radak's bridge and mark it "3."

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a line on the left and right bank of the River Lasva, first to show where Dragan Papic and the others were keeping guard, approximately. Could you mark this "4." Then could you draw another line on the other side and mark it "5." This is the position where you kept guard or patrolled the bridge.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. This photograph is upside down in relation to the panel, but you seem to be doing well in finding these places. I would now like to ask the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D23/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, what does this photograph show? What can we see here? First tell us from which side this was taken?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: This was taken from Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you see in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I can see the road leading to the bridge. I can see the River Lasva, and then I can see the houses of Pero Ljubas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a line to show where your village patrol moved.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Does it have to be a line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, a line, approximately. Did you have any trenches there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There was a trench here (marks), another trench here (marks), because this building wasn't there at the time, and there was a third trench here (marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other side Papic Vidovic and two Vidovics were patrolling?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, Dragan and Ivo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a line where they moved?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: This is where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now show us the house or the area where they rested?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: They rested in this new house (indicating), there is a big garage door here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Here it is (marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is where they rested. Very well. Now, I would like to call upon the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D24/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, what does this photograph show and where was it taken from?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: This was taken from the Vitez side toward the side of Donja Rovna and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this road --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Leads from Vitez toward Busovaca, to Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you continued up this road, where would you come to, what place?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: You would again come out on the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what village, to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, to Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you put an "X" where Radak's bridge is.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can we see on the other side? Who do these buildings belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: The buildings on the other side belong to Busovaca. This is Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We have another photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D25/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, where was this taken from?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: This was taken from Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can we see here?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: We can see the bridge, we can see the left side -- the left bank of the River Lasva, the bridge, and the houses of the late Pero Ljubas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around the garage door where they rested, because it's seen better here than in the other picture. Could you mark Radak's bridge with an "X."

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you try to explain to the Court why Radak's bridge had to be guarded?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Radak's bridge was to be guarded because the communication from Busovaca to Vitez had been cut off at Buhine Kuce where the Muslims had set up a roadblock and machine guns, so that the communication between Busovaca and Vitez was cut off on the main motorway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To avoid any misunderstanding, was it really a barricade or --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: It was machine gunfire, which cut the road, and this went on for a month, a month and a half, I can't remember exactly. So that this road and Radak's bridge was now very important strategically because the road between Busovaca and Vitez was now along the right -- through over this bridge along the right bank of the River Lasva. This was the only communication between Busovaca and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that had it not been for Radak's bridge, Vitez would have been cut off completely?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Ivo Vidovic and Dragan Vidovic kept guard with Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how Dragan Papic was dressed and armed then?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I think that then too he may have had a camouflage jacket, but I cannot remember what kind of trousers he had, but most probably it was jeans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weapons did he have?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: He had a M-48 rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything special on his face at that time, what was evident?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say, but you may be referring to the beard Dragan always wore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see Dragan now. Does he have a beard now?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he has a little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a bigger beard then, a longer one?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was much longer then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Papic was employed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Papic was employed in the Vitez forestry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know until when he worked there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, Dragan worked there until about the end -- or the beginning of the war. Not the end, but the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So until the 16th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say how long you kept guard?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I kept guard until the 12th of June, 1993. That was when I was wounded by the army of BiH, by the Muslims, and after that I was no longer active.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you seriously wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was seriously wounded. I went for treatment. I had an 84, less than two millimetres. That's what the doctor said. I was operated on four times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four times?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Dragan Papic, about his conversations, his discussions? Do you know that he liked to discuss political topics, for example? Did you ever hear him talking about that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No. Dragan liked making jokes, he liked to do odd jobs, but I don't remember ever having heard that from anyone. It never happened in my presence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were keeping watch and there was no gunfire, did you sometimes cross the bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course we did. We met, we had a chat, and then we would go back to our places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever say anything against the Muslims then or did you ever hear him saying things against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Nobody spoke about the Muslims before. We were on visiting terms with the Muslims. The Muslims would come and visit me on Easter, at Christmas, ten of them would come from Ahmici, from Rovna, and when they were celebrating Bajram I would go to visit them. We were never divided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said Rovna. Did you mean Gornja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I meant Gornja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan's father, Ivo?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his job; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: He was a plumber. He worked in Princip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he on good terms with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he is still doing plumbing for Muslims. And before the war, well, the mosque that was being built in Ahmici, he did all the plumbing there. He did it as a gift to the mosque. He did not ask for any payment. I know because I was married next to the mosque. My wife was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your wife lived near the mosque before she married you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he did this free of charge?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a donation to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war did you remain on good terms with the Muslims, many of them have come back?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they have come back. When I meet them we say "hello," there are two or three with whom I stop and chat, but you see what this cursed war has brought us. So we discuss that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, on the 16th of April, 1993, that all the Muslims left Ahmici or did any of them stay behind?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Almost all of them left, but Dervis Ahmic stayed behind, and his son, who is married to a Croatian woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find out later about what really happened in Ahmici? What did you hear? You were keeping guard, but you must have heard later what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that houses have been set on fire, that a lot of people had been killed, houses destroyed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any Croats were killed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, of course. Of course Croats were killed. Not as many as there were Muslims, but some Croats were killed too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. I request that Exhibits D23/5 (sic) to D25/5 be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection from the Prosecution. They are admitted into evidence. Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I announce Defence counsel Luka Susak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I think there is an error regarding my proposals for admission into evidence of exhibits. The number should be D22/5 through to D25/5, because I think there's an error. The first document mentioned is D23. It should be D22. From D22 to D25 inclusive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, Counsel Puliselic. Yes. So Counsel Susak will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I only have two questions for this witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Susak:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke today about Dragan Papic. Could you tell us whether he was a member of the village guards and where he patrolled, where he kept watch duty? Was he a member of the village guards?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you because I don't know, but I don't think so because he was a forester. He was working in the Sumarija company, so he spent a lot of time doing his work. As far as I know about his occupation, he must have been doing that kind of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as I understand, you're not sure that he was a member of the village guards?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, a forester, during the war was it dangerous to go through the woods?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there were troops in the woods during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Should a forester go through the woods when there were troops there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, probably not. Probably he didn't go there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where didn't he go?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: He didn't go through the woods during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what branch of the army he served when he did his regular military service?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know that he did his military service in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does a person need to be trained to use a mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the event of war, if a person is issued a weapon may he be issued another kind of weapon than the one he was trained to use?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, out of necessity probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned today what Dragan Papic told you and you remember that well. Could you tell us the story how he met with Nenad Santic and where?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know where they met. He just told me that Nenad Santic had told him to go there. I know that Nenad Santic was in charge of the village guards on their side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Papic a member of the same village guards as Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not probably, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I think yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he told you nothing else about the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill? Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Santic. My name is Michael Blaxill, I'm one of the Prosecutors in this case. I do have just a few questions for you as a result of what you've been saying here this morning. Now, where you lived, how far was that from the home of Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: About 700 or 800 metres, up to 1.000. I never measured it so I can't be very precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask in a different way: How far was it if you actually had to walk rather than just in a straight line? The actual route, do you know how far that was?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: It took about roughly 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About 20 minutes between your home and his home on foot?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Perhaps even a little less, but roughly that would be it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I noticed, sir, that for the purposes of looking at the map you, like myself, resorted to spectacles. Do you wear those simply for things like reading or do you wear them as a normal requirement for all lengths of vision?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Only for reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said around April '92 you formed the village guards in your own particular village; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was a village guard totally separate from the village guards formed over towards Zume and Santici by Mr. Nenad Santic and his neighbours there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was separate, separate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I may just confirm, sir. How many members did your guard have, your village guard, at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There may have been eight, maybe ten on the outside, men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the earlier part in '92, did you, in fact, perform a sort of 24-hour guard, or did you just guard in the night or something of that nature?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: In '92 guard duty was kept only at night, from 10.00 in the evening, 22.00 hours, until about 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of you would form a guard for a particular night-shift?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Roughly -- our shifts would be three or four hours. Four men one night, four men the next night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Probably I am just being obtuse and not fully understanding. You said you would actually do the whole of the hours of darkness. So that would be through a whole night. So when you say your shifts are four hours, do you mean that one shift would do four hours in that night and then the next shift would come on and do the other fours hours or so through the night?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Yes, we would take turns. The village was a small one. We didn't have many men, so the night hours we would share. One would arrive late at night and stay until 5.00 or 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And presumably the Radak bridge was part of that area that you would patrol during that time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many nights a week would you personally, as an individual member of the guard, be required to perform that duty?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you as an individual or any other member of the guard as an individual, how many times a week would they have to do a night's guard? Would you do it once a week, four times a week?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Every other night four men would be on guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many nights a week did you find yourself doing as a regular duty?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Roughly three nights it would be me with another three men, and then the other three nights would be another four men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, moving to the 20th of October, 1992, you returned home. Did you stay in your house for the rest of the day?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed in the house, but I went out too, outside the house, because the gunfire lasted for a long time. I went to Njive where Dragan Papic was, and then I would come home and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how far is Njive from your home, in walking distance?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, about a hundred, a hundred and fifty metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as regards the events in the Ahmici area on the 20th of October, you have stated to this court that, of course, you have no direct personal knowledge of those events because you weren't there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there and I can't say, but I've already told you what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, sir, we won't go over that again. You said that it was about 08.00 that Mr. Dragan Papic arrived near your house. That's correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. I may be 10 or 15 minutes off the mark, but around 8.00 anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he set up his mortar obviously about a hundred metres from your home?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: A hundred or a hundred and fifty metres south of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And when was it in that day that you saw Dragan Papic again after your encounter at 8.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It could have been about 11.00 or 12.00 when I went to Njive again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you say he then came back down from that position at about 4.00 in the afternoon and it had been totally quiet all day?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there had been no firing or no --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There was no firing at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did anyone from the HVO, or anybody military or with a weapon turn up on the following day, the 21st of October, and come back to that position?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did Mr. Dragan Papic tell you where he had got the mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: He told me that Nenad Santic had given it to him. That's what he told me in the morning already, and that he had sent him to go to Njive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were not home when the people came to collect the mortar a couple of days later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I wasn't. I went to work. I didn't go on the 20th of October, that day only, but the next day I already went back to work because everything was quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I'm just looking at the time. I'm moving on to an entirely different subject. It might make a natural break period to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, I said just before the break I was moving to a new topic, but there's just one final question I would like to ask you, on reflection, relating to the 20th of October. Can you say how many more visits you made to Njive in the course of that day after 11.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps about 1.00. I stayed a while and then I went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So those were the occasions that day that you saw Mr. Dragan Papic, around 11.00, around 1.00 and around 4.00, obviously after your first meeting at 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Now, in January 1993 you state that as a result of the conflict in the Busovaca area you stepped up the conduct of the guard, the village guard. What, in fact, did you do to intensify the actions of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, we sought to protect the whole village, particularly the area facing the Muslim villages, Pezici, Gornja Rovna and Kovaci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you, in fact, increase your guards in numbers or did you just increase in the amount of territory that you patrolled?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, the number was increased. Some older men joined in. After this happened in Busovaca it became more dangerous, so there were at least ten of us every night, maybe even more, to ensure security each night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, did you operate as a group of ten, or did you divide into smaller squads to carry out your patrols?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, we divided up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact still follow the four-man patrol squads that you had used before?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, we increased the number to ten or even twelve men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would actually patrol together as one group; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to be clear I understand you, sir. You have stated that on the 15th of April, all was calm, but you heard firing starting very early the following morning, the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the time that you noticed the firing? Did you check the time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: We noticed the firing about 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much longer after that was it that you encountered Mr. Dragan Papic and his family?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I was at the bridge, the Radak bridge, and Dragan came by with his wife. He stayed there just for about ten minutes, until he put them up in my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also you had stated that you had noticed the firing at about 6.00 and your next reference is to being at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got up, what was the first thing you did, having heard the firing?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't get up. I was already -- we were on guard, in the night guards. We got to the bridge when we heard the fire because our priority was to protect the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that that was the priority? Was this something that you as a group realised was a necessity, or had you received some form of instructions or orders from someone?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I received -- I received orders to make sure to watch over Radak's bridge during the night patrols, and also the right bank of the Lasva River, which belongs to Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did your orders come from, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: My orders came from Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that an HVO headquarters in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you went to the bridge; about what time do you recall arriving at the Radak bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: About 6.00, a couple of minutes after 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you've already told us a few minutes later Mr. Dragan Papic appeared. Now --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He went to stay at -- I believe you said your brother's house, the Papic family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, that is correct, at my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he had settled his womenfolk, Mr. Papic returned to the bridge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you confirmed that he came obviously from your direction, at your village, across the bridge to join Mr. Ivo Vidovic on the other side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew Mr. Vidovic, I presume?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew both Vidovics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because I believe there was a third man there that was Mr. Dragan Vidovic; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you -- how many other people were actually serving with you at that time when you started duty at the bridge on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: At that moment, there were three men with me on the right-hand bank of the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, sir, who they were?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Out of the ten or so men, it could have been Zoran Santic, Jozo Alilovic, Pero Alilovic. I think it was the three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to the best of your recollection, they were the three men who were with you in the early morning of the 16th of April '93?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you seem a little hesitant; your memory is not entirely certain? Would that be so?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I'm certain that they were there. It was most probable that the -- the three of them with me. I had ten men with me, and then they were dispersed to other places. But Jozo Alilovic never moved away, because these others were less serious, and we had to make sure that no sabotage activities could take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So having dispersed some of the members of the ten-man guard, how many of you took up position at the end of the bridge, if I can use that expression?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: At the end of the bridge, there was me and three other men. Three other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are the three gentlemen you've named the three soldiers you recall being with you at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you remain in that position, at that location, that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: That morning I stayed all day and all night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time, yourself, leave the location to go and seek refreshment or take rest?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. They would bring us refreshment and food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- was there any firing that was causing a danger to yourself and your fellow guards at that point and at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: There was shooting; there were all kinds of things, and we didn't dare move around. We just had to keep quiet so as to give ourselves a chance to take a rest, to take a breather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I presume I could suggest that -- did you keep yourselves under cover as best you could, either in a trench, or behind some form of protection?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were under cover in trenches, because there were three trenches on the right-hand side of the Lasva River, as I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe the activities of the guards on the other side of the bridge, namely Mr. Papic and the two gentlemen by the name of Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they in fact take cover and keep their heads down? Were they in some similar danger?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: They also had two trenches, and the third -- there were only three of them on the other side of the bridge -- they stayed in the house of Pero Ljubas, so one was resting and two of them were on the left-hand bank of the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And presumably in what was obviously a hazardous position for some days at that bridge, both at your side of the bridge and their side of the bridge, you would keep yourself very much under cover; that would be sensible. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as the days would unfold, the second and the third and the fourth day, you would, would you not, rotate yourselves to go off and take some rest?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course we did. Those of us who were on the Donja Rovna side, we had sufficient soldiers, and there were no attacks against Donja Rovna. We just had to watch over the Radak bridge, which was strategically important, and we had to look after it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I can encapsulate the point at this time, certainly on that first day, the 16th of April, you were out of sight of the guards on the other side of the bridge, and they were out of your sight for periods of time, because presumably you were taking cover from the danger that was present; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: It is true that we could see each other. We couldn't get out of the trenches, but we could see each other. At least those who were on duty at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But of course as well during the day, people were -- in the case of those guards, the other side, going to the house for rest; and as for your guards, were you going back to your own homes to take rest?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: My guards went home too, but they were protected by the willow trees. But I didn't leave for 20, maybe 30 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you find safe shelter to take a rest from your guard duty?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: We went to our houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry; I thought you said that you didn't have the shelter, so that you stayed for about 30 hours. Did you not take rest during those 30 hours when you stayed on guard?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I did not at all. I didn't take any rest. My soldiers did, but I didn't, because I couldn't allow it. As the commander of this group of people, I couldn't leave them, and in case something should happen for which I would be made responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that first day, and as we go over the subsequent days, did conditions allow for you in fact to take rest at home and be away from the bridge for a while?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Later I could move away, because I had a reliable older man, and he was Jozo Alilovic. So he would take over when I went to rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long would your rest periods last? I mean, was it a regular thing, or did it -- only a few hours at a time? Was it a strict routine, or not?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No. When you felt sleepy, you could have a nap for two, three, sometimes four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course at those times you'd be away from the bridge, so you would not know the whereabouts of the guards on the other end of the bridge as such, because you wouldn't be there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. When I was away, I couldn't see them then, but my colleague who replaced me could see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if for any reason, either by way of orders or for whatever reason, one of them might have slipped away from the position, and if your colleague didn't tell you about it, you would not have known; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think during the first few days it was possible to leave guard duty, especially on the Vitez side of the Lasva River, because the shooting was coming from that side. So that even if there was time, people could not leave those positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, from the photographs we have seen there appear to be buildings and foliage and trees, so I suppose a soldier or a guard could try and slip away from the position without being shot? It's a possibility, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it is possible, but as far as I know, I think the order was that no one should move away, even if it was possible. But I believe that it was not possible to pass and reach the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, over the next few days, you were aware from personal observations of the presence of Mr. Dragan Papic as one of the guards at that bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall the date when he left that location?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I do not recall the date. That is why I said that for seven, eight, or ten days, he was there on guard duty. I would see him there. After that, he left; I heard that his wife had had a baby. And then he didn't come back until the time I was wounded. Where he went, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point is, sir, you have suggested with some certainty of the 24-hour presence of Mr. Dragan Papic, and you say that this was by virtual constant observation, but you don't in fact recall the exact number of days that you made these observations; you're not certain whether it was seven days, eight, nine, or ten days that he was actually at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: At least seven days. I didn't count the days. Maybe even ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course he was in a different chain of command to yourself so you would not be aware of any orders he received or instructions or, indeed, any discipline exerted by his commander; is that right? It wasn't your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that, but as far as we discussed these things, when we had the time he said that they weren't allowed to go anywhere, that they had secured Pero Ljubas's house so that the person who was resting could go to that house. But otherwise they had to keep watch duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, I am going to just ask you a few names of persons. I believe they may have been people based in the Busovaca command, as it were, and I just wonder if you recognise these names. Mr. Zdravko Prankovic, does that name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a Mr. Stipica Santic, Stipica Santic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: From Busovaca? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A Zeljko Grbavac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Dragan, yes, I know Dragan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ivica Krizanac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just a moment to confer, if I may, Your Honours, and then I believe I might be able to conclude quickly. Thank you, Your Honours. I do have just one or two further matters. Your colleague, Mr. Santic, Mr. Dragan Vidovic, who was serving, I believe, the other end of the bridge, did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Dragan? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me how old he was, at that time, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Dragan Papic -- Dragan Vidovic, maybe 24, 25, 26. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his father's name was, Dragan's father?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: I do. Franjo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Franjo. Thank you. Do you know where they lived, their address, or at least close to their street or something?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Santici. The upper part of Santici. I don't know how else I could explain it. Also known as Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Whilst you were doing your guard duty at the bridge, the Radak bridge, did you receive orders still via or from the Busovaca HVO, HQ?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: No. There were some tours, they would come to see whether everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: And then they would say, "Yes, that's fine, be careful," and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These would be tours by HVO personnel from Busovaca? Yes? Busovaca. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. About how many times did they come? Was it once a week or every couple of days? Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SANTIC
utterances.text: Every two or three days. It depended. Sometimes they would come during the night for checkup.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I am obliged. Thank you very much, Your Honours. That concludes the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't have any questions either. Mr. Santic, thank you for giving evidence in Court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your welcome. Thank you too. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Now, we could just use this few minutes just to go through some housekeeping matters. First of all, we would like to let you know the schedule for the next few months. I think you already know about February, March and April, and April as well, and May as well. May, I may remember, I may remind you, that in May we will sit from the 3rd to the 7th and then from the 25th to the 28th. 24th is -- I think it's a holiday. So 25th, which is Tuesday, through 28th. Then again on the 31st of May. Now, let us now move to June. June, from the 1st to the 4th, and then from the 21st through to 29th. After that we have a Plenary Session of the Tribunal. We will reconvene in July, on the 5th of July for three weeks, from the 5th to the 23rd of July, and we very much hope that the Defence may conclude their case by the 23rd of July. We have set aside two weeks in September, from the 13th to the 24th, for closing statements and, if need be, for any rebuttal evidence. The 13th, 24th. So that if we conclude, finish on the 24th, we may be able in three months to draft and deliver our judgment before Christmas, before the end of December. We will need a minimum of three months, of course. All right. Any comments? You may appreciate that we, of course, have other cases. Any comments from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. If there are no other matters, we may adjourn now. So we adjourn until next Wednesday at 9.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
